headline: Foundation model pretraining across imaging, MEG, and molecular property prediction
label: Foundation Model Representation Learning
summary: Recent preprints examine how pretraining data, tokenization, and multimodal fusion determine transfer in biomedical foundation models.
synthesis: The common thread is reuse of pretrained or multimodal representations for downstream biomedical prediction, with transfer evaluated across heterogeneous modalities. RaSD pretrains medical image foundation models entirely on randomized synthetic data and evaluates them across 56 downstream tasks and 48 datasets. A systematic comparison of sample-level tokenizers for transformer-based MEG foundation models includes learnable and non-learnable options and introduces an autoencoder tokenizer. TITAN-BBB fuses tabular, image, and text features via attention to predict blood-brain barrier permeability. MolDeBERTa is a chemistry-informed self-supervised SMILES encoder pretrained on up to 123M PubChem molecules, improving MoleculeNet property prediction. What is new is the focus on how pretraining data source, tokenization, and fusion design shape transfer. The items do not share a common benchmark, so cross-item comparisons should be made cautiously.
